_meta.project: instex Spectrograph Explorer presets -- round 7: Lick Observatory Shane 3-m / Hamilton Echelle Spectrometer (coude focus; iodine-cell planet search); new glass SCHOTT UBK7 (secondary source)
_meta.rule: Every value carries src (key into sources), loc and a short verbatim quote from the saved document. DERIVED = arithmetic done here from sourced values; INFERRED = a reading the source does not state; MEASURED = read from a figure with a known scale (method stated); SCHEMATIC = no scale. alternatives = other sourced values (conflicts). Quotes whose first word is FIG: are figure readings, not text quotes; scan=True marks quotes whose digits were transcribed from the page image.
_meta.normalization: whitespace, case, hyphens and hyphenation, quotes, dashes and minus signs, micro and mu signs, degree signs and the OCR '?' for a degree-decimal glyph, ligatures and the tilde operator are normalized; ' ... ' joins non-adjacent pieces; PDFs are compared with pdftotext -layout and -raw text, HTML with tag-stripped text.

echelle_geometry_alpha_beta.derived: INFERRED: the sources do not say which side is the larger angle. The published magnification -22 requires (f_col/f_cam) / [cos(alpha)/cos(beta)] = 14.71 / [cos(alpha)/cos(beta)] = 22, i.e. cos(alpha)/cos(beta) = 0.669 (alpha = 70.2, beta = 59.2: 0.6615, M = 22.23); the opposite assignment gives M = 9.7. The table's dispersions (3.20 A/mm at order 100, 1.96 at order 163, 5.61 at order 57) also need cos(beta) = 0.512 (beta = 59.2): a cos(beta) / (m f_cam) = 31746 nm x 0.512 / (100 x 508.3 mm) = 3.198 A/mm (table: 3.20). The explorer's convention is the same (alpha = blaze + theta, M2FS and MIKE records).

grating_equation_check.unit: nm (m x lambda at blaze center)
grating_equation_check.derived: DERIVED: m lambda = a (sin alpha + sin beta) = (10^6 / 31.5 nm) x (sin 70.2 + sin 59.2) = 31746 x (0.94066 + 0.85897) = 57,138 nm; order 100 blazes at 571.38 nm, the table's 5713.8 A (HOR) and Vogt's 5714 A (Table I).

hamilton.layout_summary: Element order (V87 Fig. 1, HFIG, HOPT): slit (aperture plate) -> shutter and filter wheel -> off-axis parabolic collimator (turns 11 deg; slit off axis) -> echelle (in plane, 2 theta = 11 deg, so the dispersed beam returns past the collimator beam alongside the main I-beam) -> two UBK7 prisms -> Schmidt corrector -> 40 deg fold flat (with hole) -> spherical camera mirror -> back through the hole's field flattener -> CCD dewar. Both the echelle and the camera fold lie in the same horizontal plane in the top view, the cross-dispersion is vertical. Explorer layout inputs: layLen (collimator to echelle) 5400 mm MEASURED, camLen (echelle to the corrector) 2500 mm MEASURED, colTilt 5.5 deg (INFERRED from the 11 deg deviation; OFF-AXIS), cam 'mirror' (catadioptric).

conflicts.text: 31.6 /mm actual (V87 p. 1220, p. 1218; FT94) vs 31.5 /mm modeled (V87 Fig. 2, Table I; HQR). The preset uses 31.5 because Vogt says only 31.5 with 43.4 deg reproduces the format.

45 deg design (V87 p. 1219) vs 44.8 deg actual (V87 p. 1220) vs 43.4 deg effective (V87 Fig. 2, Table I) vs 43.9 deg (HQR). 43.4 reproduces the tabulated order separations to 0.4-1.7%; 43.9 to 2-3%; 44.8 to 5-6% (DERIVED).
204 mm (V87 text, 8 inch) vs 207.0 mm (V87 Table I) vs 8.15 inch = 207 mm (FT94) vs 208.4 mm (HQR). Spread 2%; the preset uses 208.4 (f_col / W = 35.87 equals the f/36 feed).

V87: 204 x 408 mm (8 x 16 inch); FT94: 8 x 12 inch. UNRESOLVED footprint problem: with alpha = 70.2 deg on the collimator side (needed for the published -22 and the dispersions) a 208.4 mm beam covers 208.4 / cos(70.2) = 615 mm of the echelle, more than 408 mm; the other assignment (alpha = 59.2: 407 mm) fits the 408 mm length exactly but gives magnification -9.7 and 2.1 A/mm at order 100. The sources do not discuss it; the preset follows the dispersion and magnification evidence.

V87 Table I, order 100: 0.23 mm = 6.47 arcsec (28.1 arcsec/mm at the detector; geometry gives 27.8) vs HOR, same order: 0.231 mm = 6.898 arcsec (29.9 arcsec/mm, +7%). The arcsec column of the manual is not consistent with its own f_col, f_cam and 1.89 arcsec/mm; the scored value uses the geometry.

R = 30,000 (V87, 1987, TI chip) / 40,000 (F14, MB92, before 1994) / 62,000 (B96, after the 1994 camera upgrade; 'intrinsic' 120,000) / 64,000 (F14, Dewar 13, 1.2 arcsec, measured) / 47,000 (Dewar 6) / 56,000 (Dewar 8) / 'about 60,000-100,000 depending on the detector' (HIN) / 50,000-115,000 (F14, by decker). The slit-limited model for 1.2 arcsec is 62,560 (DERIVED).

MB92: 3800-9500 A in ~100 orders on the Ford chip; F14: the Ford format spanned 4850-6700 A, Dewar 13's 4850-9362 A; HNV: the 2048 chips capture 'virtually the entire useful spectrum'. The format is a setting (dewar height and grating tilt); the sum of the order separations (28.5 mm) fits a 30.72 mm chip.
HCC: narrow-slit FWHM ~2.2 px (Dewar 6) vs ~1.45 px (Dewar 8); F14: R = 47,000 (Dewar 6), 56,000 (Dewar 8), 64,000 (Dewar 13) with the 1.2 arcsec slit.

notes: THE RECOMMENDED SETTING is the planet-search configuration with the Dewar 13 CCD (1994 Nov camera upgrade to Feb 1998): it is the era whose resolution was published as R = 62,000 (B96) and measured as 64,000 (F14), and the narrowest line profile of the program (Dewar 6 and Dewar 8 broaden it by charge diffusion, which the explorer does not model). The geometry is the same for every detector era; only the pixel format changes.

The Hamilton's central wavelength in the iodine region is chosen (5500 A) rather than sourced: the format is a setting. The iodine cell, the collimator mask and the 600 um (1.13 arcsec) slit are not drawn.
The 11 deg turn at the collimator and the 11 deg between the collimator and camera beams at the echelle are the same angle by design (V87: the dispersed beam runs alongside the main I-beam).

The explorer's model cannot represent: the pre-1994 asymmetric profile; charge diffusion of the thinned and deep-depletion chips; the echelle footprint (a beam wider than the ruled length); the order curvature the manual mentions; the collimator mask; a catadioptric camera's central obstruction (the Schmidt's fold flat with its hole).
The Hamilton is also fed by the 0.6-m CAT with the same f/36 beam but 9.45 arcsec/mm (HQR); a CAT preset is the same optics with D = 0.6 m (not recommended).
The manual's 'Slit on Detector 330 um/pixel' is a magnification statement (22:1 in the dispersion direction), not a slit length.

UBK7.formula: Sellmeier_SCHOTT: n^2 - 1 = sum B_i lambda^2/(lambda^2 - C_i), lambda in um
